- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then sharply decline, suggesting overshoot after spikes.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias — forecasts drift toward historical lows after initial spikes, but not fast enough to match true price corrections.
- Forecast horizon (30d) shows persistent lag: true prices often dip below forecast mid-point before rebounding, indicating model under-reacts to short-term volatility.
- Model fails to capture downward momentum in late 30d window — often overestimates prices when true values are trending lower.
- Forecasts are overly optimistic in high-price regimes (e.g., >70) and under-react to policy or supply shocks.
- Model exhibits “sticky” behavior — once a price spike occurs, forecasts remain elevated longer than true prices adjust.
- Model underestimates volatility in early 30d window, leading to under-shock responses in price drops.
- Forecasts show diminishing sensitivity to recent history — model ignores recent low prices when forecasting future values.
